name: @everfur/mcp

tools.name: everfur_plan_integration
tools.description: Produce an integration plan for a project. REFUSES underspecified input by naming the missing facts rather than guessing them, and REFUSES a project shape the SDK ships no entry point for (PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED) or a capability set the contract blocks outright (CAPABILITIES_BLOCKED). Read-only. Reads the contract from GET /partners/contract with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY unless contract_path or EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC names a projection file.

project_root.description: For a local MCP only: absolute path to the application root. Pass exactly one of this or project_details.

project_details.description: For a remote MCP only: a safe projection of package dependencies, package manager, and fixed file-presence markers. Pass exactly one of this or project_root; never send source files, env files, or credentials.

theme_source.description: For a remote MCP: the text of the project's tailwind.config.{js,ts}, the CSS that declares its theme (a Tailwind v4 @theme block or :root custom properties), or a React Native theme or colours file, so the plan can match the generated surface to the project's own theme. Read statically and never executed. With project_root the project is read from disk instead; this argument, when given, wins. The plan refuses to guess a theme it cannot read and names the missing facts in its match-theme step.

capabilities.description: Which Everfur capabilities this integration uses, as the contract names them. The ids the contract can plan today are "chat", "entitlements", "events", "notifications", "photo", "records", "records-clinic" and "televet"; "animations", "records-push", "records-transfer", "server-pets" and "video" are blocked today and a plan refuses them with the reason. Pass ["all"] for every plannable capability. The loaded contract is the authority: an UNKNOWN_OPTION refusal lists its exact ids. The plan holds no credential, so everfur_verify_integration (not this tool) is the fail-closed check of what the tenant actually has. Omit if unknown; the tool will refuse and list the ids.

identity_mode.description: anonymous = no backend, scoped to the device. partner-user-ref = your backend mints a session against your own user id. shopify-app-proxy = a Shopify storefront, where Shopify vouches for the signed-in customer and no partner backend mints. "personalized" is accepted as an alias for partner-user-ref.

session_mint_language.description: Backend language that will mint sessions. Only meaningful when identity_mode is partner-user-ref.

embedding.description: For a web project only: "in-page" mounts the SDK's React components in the page (detected when package.json declares react-dom), "frame" includes the loader and renders the surface in an iframe on Everfur's origin (detected otherwise). Omit to accept what the project says; pass it to override.

environment.description: The Everfur deployment the generated configuration targets: staging (your sandbox tenant, a pk_live_ key, livemode false; "test" names the same deployment) or production. Required for a plan that writes code; never assumed. Ask the developer. On the Everfur-hosted server an omitted environment is the connected tenant's, and one naming a different host is refused (ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH).

contract_path.description: Path to a contract-public projection. Defaults to EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC, then to the contract fetched from the Everfur API with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY.

tools.name: everfur_verify_integration
tools.description: Mint a session, poll entitlements, and hard-assert the verdict is not empty; optionally exercise the chat, records, televet and theme surfaces and check the project on disk. With identity_mode anonymous it verifies the anonymous path instead (the publishable key and a derived session id, the conversation list, and whether the tenant requires signed sessions). Returns PASS/SKIP/FAIL/GATED per step with the request id of the call that produced it. Mints a real session, and on a sandbox tenant only a real Televet handoff, so it is not read-only; it sends no write to a live tenant.

user_ref.description: End-user id to mint the test session for. Defaults to a CLI-owned value.

identity_mode.description: The identity to verify with. "partner-user-ref" (the default): a signed session. "anonymous": the publishable key and a device session id derived from user_ref, exactly what an anonymous integration sends; nothing is minted, the verdict and the conversation list are read on that identity, and the tenant's sessions_required policy is reported (it refuses only a publishable-key caller that asserts x-everfur-user-ref; pure anonymous chat keeps working).

attempts.description: How many times to read the verdict before concluding it is empty.

origin.description: For a web integration: the page origin the surface is embedded on, e.g. https://shop.example.com. Adds the web checks: the CORS preflight, the embed fence for that origin, CORS exposure of X-Request-ID and Retry-After, whether the tenant requires signed sessions, and that the loader pairing with the configured API is reachable.

loader_url.description: With origin: the loader to probe instead of the one derived from EVERFUR_API_BASE_URL (https, or http on localhost). Without it a local or unrecognised API reports the loader check as not checked.

surfaces.description: Surfaces to exercise with the minted session. chat and records: the diagnostics reason, then a read on the session. televet: mints a real vet visit handoff, on a SANDBOX tenant only (never a live one); the one-time token is never returned. theme: the branding the verdict carries, judged with the SDK's own rules, merged with the theme prop everfur_plan_integration writes when project_root or theme_source is given. A surface Everfur has not switched on is reported GATED, not FAIL. With identity_mode anonymous, chat is read on the anonymous identity and records and televet are skipped: both take a signed session only.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the application root. Adds offline project checks: no partner secret key in source or client build output, no secret behind a NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ prefix, the secret read only by server code, 'use client' on Next.js App Router files importing the SDK, and that the env files name the same API host this verify ran against. File contents are never returned.

theme_source.description: With the theme surface: the same text everfur_plan_integration takes as theme_source (the project's tailwind config, the CSS that declares its theme, or a React Native theme or colours file). The branding is judged merged with the theme prop the plan writes from it, as the SDK merges them. Read statically and never executed; when given, it wins over project_root.

annotations.title: Verify the wire end to end

tools.name: everfur_diagnose
tools.description: Separate the four byte-identical causes of an empty entitlement verdict. Read-only. Reports honestly when the deployment does not serve the diagnostics route rather than relaying a bare 404. With bundle: true, returns one support bundle (project, framework, SDK and CLI versions, contract digest, credential presence without values, and the diagnosis request id) whatever state the integration is in.

bundle.description: Return one support bundle instead of the diagnosis alone: project and framework, @everfur/sdk and CLI versions, the contract digest, which credentials are set (names and public prefixes, never values), and the diagnosis with its request id. Produced whatever state the integration is in; give it to the developer for a support ticket.

project_root.description: With bundle: absolute path to the application root to describe. Never defaulted; without it the bundle reports the project as not read.

annotations.title: Explain why a capability is unavailable

tools.name: everfur_explain_error
tools.description: Explain a wire error code: cause, whether it is retryable, and the next action. Reads the registry from the contract. The contract is fetched with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY unless contract_path or EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC names a projection file. Needs no project. REFUSES a code the registry does not list, with near misses, rather than inventing an explanation from the shape of the string.

code.description: The wire error code, exactly as the response carried it. CASE SENSITIVE: three naming families are live at once, so `authExpired` and `AuthorizationException` are two different 401s and `authexpired` is neither.

contract_path.description: Path to a contract-public projection to read the registry from. Defaults to EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC, then to the contract fetched from the Everfur API with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY.

annotations.title: Explain an Everfur API error code

tools.name: everfur_send_test_message
tools.description: Send a REAL message and stream a real veterinary answer, against a SANDBOX tenant only. Refuses unless the entitlement verdict reports livemode false. Returns the answer plus a frame histogram, so a stream that died mid-answer is distinguishable from a short one. Asks with a signed session when one is available, and with pet_profile registers a sandbox pet first so the answer is pet-aware. Calling again with the same idempotency_key reuses that conversation and returns the existing answer instead of sending a second message.

message.description: What to ask. A real pet-health question gets a real answer.

idempotency_key.description: Required and explicit. A call with a key and message already sent reuses that conversation and returns its stored answer instead of sending again. This is done by the tool reading the conversation first; the server does not deduplicate sends.

pet_ref.description: Optional pet to scope the conversation to. Must already be registered for this identity, unless pet_profile is passed, which registers it.

pet_profile.description: Optional sandbox pet to register for this call's identity before the send (under pet_ref, else a fixed test ref), so the answer is scoped to it. Registered only once the sandbox fence has passed.

annotations.title: Send a real message against a sandbox tenant

instructions:
Everfur partner integration tools.

Everfur is a pet-health API. Partners embed chat, medical-records and Televet (vet visit) surfaces in their own apps and pages
via @everfur/sdk (React Native and Expo; the web through @everfur/sdk/web and a hosted frame; Flutter
through everfur_sdk). On the web the plan follows the contract: a React tree embeds the SDK in the page,
any other page includes the loader and gets the frame, and a Shopify storefront gets the Everfur app's
theme block with Shopify vouching for the signed-in customer (identity_mode shopify-app-proxy). A
capability the web cannot render (photo in the page, anything but chat in the frame) is reported as
blocked by the platform; do not substitute the React Native entry points and do not invent an
integration from the HTTP routes.

Use everfur_plan_integration FIRST. Describe the project with project_root when this server runs on the same
machine as the project, or with project_details (package dependencies, package manager and file-presence markers,
never source files or credentials) when this is a remote MCP that cannot read the project. The plan matches the
generated surface to the project's own theme (a Tailwind v4 @theme block, tailwind.config, :root custom properties,
a React Native theme file), read statically and never executed; a remote MCP passes that text as theme_source.
When the theme cannot be read the plan says so in its match-theme step and never guesses one. It refuses
underspecified input by naming exactly which facts are missing. When it refuses, ask the developer those specific questions and call it again. Do not guess the
answers and do not proceed without them: an integration built on a guessed identity mode is wrong in a way
that only shows up in production.

Then everfur_verify_integration to exercise the real wire, and everfur_diagnose when a working integration
stops returning capabilities. Verification uses EVERFUR_SESSION_TOKEN, a short-lived session the partner's backend
minted for a test user; EVERFUR_PARTNER_SECRET_KEY never belongs in this server's environment and is never read by
it. When the session step is skipped, ask the developer to mint a session on their backend and set it. An anonymous
integration is verified with identity_mode anonymous instead: the publishable key and a derived session id, with
nothing minted.

Whenever an Everfur response carries an error code, call everfur_explain_error with that code rather than
explaining it yourself. Three naming families are live at once and
one code is the default for four different HTTP statuses, so a code explained from the shape of its string
produces a confident, wrong retry policy. If the tool says the code is unknown, say so; do not fill it in.

Every tool returns structured content. A failed call carries error.code, error.retryable and
error.next_action: branch on those, not on the message. Reference material is served as resources
(everfur://guide, everfur://contract/errors, everfur://mcp/refusal-codes), and the prompts
integrate-web, integrate-react-native and diagnose-integration lay out the order to call the tools in.

The Everfur contract (the error registry, capabilities and decision trees the planner, everfur_explain_error,
the guide and the contract resources read) is served only to an authenticated partner. It is fetched with
EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY from EVERFUR_API_BASE_URL. When a tool refuses with CONTRACT_CREDENTIAL_MISSING,
tell the developer to set those variables in this server's environment; do not answer from memory instead.
The documented environment is EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY, EVERFUR_API_BASE_URL, EVERFUR_PARTNER_KEY and, for verification,
EVERFUR_SESSION_TOKEN.
